common_uses: Relief of mild to moderate pain (headache, toothache, muscle ache) and reduction of fever.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits prostaglandin synthesis in the central nervous system and acts on the hypothalamic heat-regulating center.
common_side_effects: Generally well tolerated at therapeutic doses. Rare nausea, allergic skin reaction, rash.
serious_warnings: Acute liver damage (hepatotoxicity) can occur if taken in excessive doses (exceeding 4000 mg in 24 hours for adults) or combined with alcohol. Check all combination cough/cold medications to avoid accidental overdose.
precautions: Exercise extreme caution in patients with existing chronic liver disease, severe renal impairment, or chronic alcohol dependency.
contraindications: Known severe hypersensitivity to paracetamol; severe acute active liver failure.
drug_interactions: Warfarin (prolonged regular use may enhance anticoagulant effect), Isoniazid, chronic alcohol consumption.
source_reference: US FDA Drug Safety Communication & MedlinePlus Health Information

common_uses: Relief of inflammation, swelling, stiffness, and joint pain associated with arthritis, menstrual cramps, toothache, and fever.
mechanism_of_action: Non-selectively inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2), reducing inflammatory prostaglandin synthesis.
common_side_effects: Dyspepsia, heartburn, stomach pain, mild nausea, fluid retention, dizziness.
serious_warnings: Increases risk of serious gastrointestinal adverse events including bleeding, ulceration, and perforation. NSAIDs (except aspirin) increase the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events (myocardial infarction and stroke).
precautions: Take with food or milk to minimize gastric upset. Caution in elderly patients, those with hypertension, heart failure, or renal impairment.
contraindications: Active peptic ulcer disease or GI bleeding; severe heart failure; third trimester of pregnancy; history of aspirin-induced asthma or urticaria.
drug_interactions: Aspirin, other NSAIDs, systemic corticosteroids, anticoagulants (Warfarin), ACE inhibitors, diuretics, lithium.
source_reference: FDA Medication Guide & WHO Model Formulary

common_uses: First-line pharmacological management of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus to improve glycemic control in conjunction with diet and exercise.
mechanism_of_action: Decreases hepatic glucose production, decreases intestinal absorption of glucose, and improves insulin sensitivity by increasing peripheral glucose uptake.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal bloating, flatulence, metallic taste, vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use.
serious_warnings: Lactic Acidosis: A rare but severe, life-threatening metabolic complication characterized by elevated blood lactate levels, metabolic acidosis, hypothermia, and hypotension. Risk increases with renal impairment, sepsis, and excessive alcohol.
precautions: Monitor renal function (eGFR) regularly prior to initiation and at least annually. Temporarily withhold before iodinated contrast radiological procedures.
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2); acute or chronic metabolic acidosis (including diabetic ketoacidosis); severe hypoxemia.
drug_interactions: Iodinated radiocontrast agents, alcohol, cimetidine, carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
source_reference: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care & MedlinePlus

common_uses: Treatment of essential hypertension (high blood pressure) and chronic stable angina.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits the transmembrane influx of calcium ions into vascular smooth muscle and cardiac muscle, resulting in peripheral arterial vasodilation.
common_side_effects: Peripheral peripheral edema (swelling of ankles/feet), flushing, dizziness, palpitations, fatigue, headache.
serious_warnings: May rarely precipitate symptomatic hypotension or exacerbate angina/myocardial infarction in patients with severe obstructive coronary artery disease.
precautions: Caution in patients with severe aortic stenosis or hepatic impairment (extensively metabolized by liver).
contraindications: Known severe hypersensitivity to amlodipine; severe hypotension; cardiogenic shock.
drug_interactions: Simvastatin (do not exceed 20 mg simvastatin daily), CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin), cyclosporine.
source_reference: WHO Guidelines for Pharmacological Treatment of Hypertension & FDA Label

common_uses: Relief of symptoms associated with seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis (sneezing, rhinorrhea, nasal itching) and chronic idiopathic urticaria.
mechanism_of_action: Selective peripheral histamine H1-receptor antagonist, inhibiting histamine-mediated allergic response.
common_side_effects: Mild drowsiness, dry mouth, headache, fatigue, pharyngitis.
serious_warnings: May impair mental alertness or physical coordination. Patients should avoid operating machinery or driving until response is known.
precautions: Dose adjustment required in moderate-to-severe renal impairment. Avoid concurrent alcohol consumption.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to cetirizine, hydroxyzine, or levocetirizine; end-stage renal disease (CrCl < 10 mL/min).
drug_interactions: Central nervous system depressants, alcohol, sedatives.

common_uses: Short-term treatment of active duodenal and benign gastric ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), erosive esophagitis, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
mechanism_of_action: Suppresses gastric acid secretion by specific inhibition of the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of gastric parietal cells.
common_side_effects: Headache, abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, flatulence.
serious_warnings: Prolonged use (especially over 1 year) may increase the risk of bone fractures (hip, wrist, spine), Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea, hypomagnesemia, and vitamin B12 deficiency.
precautions: Response does not preclude the presence of gastric malignancy. Take 30-60 minutes before meals for optimal absorption.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to substituted benzimidazoles; co-administration with rilpivirine-containing products.
drug_interactions: Clopidogrel (decreased antiplatelet activity), methotrexate, digoxin, diazepam, ketoconazole.

common_uses: Treatment of mild to moderate bacterial infections: community-acquired pneumonia, acute bacterial sinusitis, pharyngitis/tonsillitis, skin infections, and urethritis/cervicitis.
mechanism_of_action: Binds reversibly to the 50S ribosomal subunit of susceptible microorganisms, inhibiting protein synthesis.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, abdominal abdominal cramping, vomiting, headache.
serious_warnings: Antibiotic resistance risk: Use strictly as prescribed for verified bacterial infections. QT prolongation and risk of fatal torsades de pointes ventricular arrhythmia in susceptible patients. Hepatotoxicity and cholestatic jaundice.
precautions: Caution in patients with known prolonged QT interval, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or bradycardia.
contraindications: History of allergic reaction to azithromycin, erythromycin, or any macrolide antibiotic; prior history of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction with azithromycin.
drug_interactions: Antacids containing aluminum or magnesium (reduce peak absorption), warfarin (increased PT/INR), antiarrhythmics (amiodarone, sotalol).
source_reference: US FDA Safety Communication & WHO Guidelines

common_uses: Relief and prevention of acute bronchospasm in patients with asthma, chronic bronchitis, and other chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases (COPD).
mechanism_of_action: Selectively stimulates beta-2 adrenergic receptors in bronchial smooth muscle, causing relaxation and bronchodilation.
common_side_effects: Fine skeletal muscle tremor (especially hands), palpitations, tachycardia, nervousness, headache, dizziness.
serious_warnings: Paradoxical bronchospasm: Immediate life-threatening airway constriction may occasionally occur; if observed, discontinue immediately. Overuse indicates poorly controlled asthma requiring anti-inflammatory corticosteroid escalation.
precautions: Caution in patients with cardiovascular disorders (coronary insufficiency, hypertension), hyperthyroidism, diabetes, or epilepsy.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to salbutamol; not indicated to manage threatened abortion in unapproved clinical settings.
drug_interactions: Non-selective beta-blockers (propranolol) may block bronchodilation; potassium-depleting diuretics.

common_uses: Prevention and treatment of clinical dehydration due to acute diarrhea, cholera, vomiting, or excessive heat exhaustion.
mechanism_of_action: Sodium-glucose co-transport across the intestinal mucosal brush border accelerates water and electrolyte absorption into systemic circulation.
common_side_effects: None when diluted in the exact correct quantity of clean drinking water. Excessive concentration can cause mild hypernatremia.
serious_warnings: Always dissolve in the exact volume of drinking water indicated on the packet (standard WHO formula: 1 packet in 1 liter of water). Never mix with milk, soup, or fruit juice. Never boil after preparation.
precautions: If child or patient is unable to drink, becomes lethargic, or vomits continuously, urgent intravenous fluid rehydration is required.
contraindications: Severe intractable vomiting, paralytic ileus, bowel perforation, severe uncorrected anuria.
drug_interactions: None significant. Enhances recovery without interacting with essential medications.
source_reference: World Health Organization (WHO) & UNICEF Child Health Guidelines

common_uses: Reduction of elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, and triglycerides in primary hyperlipidemia; prevention of cardiovascular disease.
mechanism_of_action: Competitively inhibits 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in hepatic cholesterol synthesis.
common_side_effects: Nasopharyngitis, arthralgia, diarrhea, indigestion, mild transient muscle ache.
serious_warnings: Rhabdomyolysis and myopathy: Patients must immediately report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, particularly if accompanied by malaise or dark urine. Liver enzyme abnormalities.
precautions: Perform liver function tests prior to initiating therapy and when clinically indicated. Avoid excessive grapefruit juice consumption (> 1 quart daily).
contraindications: Active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases; pregnancy and breastfeeding.
drug_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, itraconazole), cyclosporine, gemfibrozil, protease inhibitors.
source_reference: AHA/ACC Cholesterol Clinical Guidelines & US FDA
